title: Solidigm Dangles New $45 Billion US Plant to Upgrade China Site
summary: Solidigm Inc., an American subsidiary of the South Korean memory-chip maker SK Hynix Inc., is in talks with the US Commerce Department to invest $45 billion in a new US chip plant, according to people familiar with the negotiations.

title: The AI Boom Will Pull Back, Warns Former SEC Chair Gary Gensler
summary: Former SEC Chair Gary Gensler says history suggests today’s AI investment boom will not continue indefinitely. He's expecting some form of slowdown or reversal within the next 18 to 30 months, and says mounting debt could determine how disruptive that correction becomes. Gensler also weighs in on interest rates, monetary policy, financial stability, and the possibility that the U.S. has overbuilt AI infrastructure. Gensler, now Professor of the Practice of Global Economics and Management at MIT's Sloan School of Management, speaks with Bloomberg Surveillance hosts Tom Keene and Paul Sweeney. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Spain Eases Data Center Energy Rules in Win for Big Tech
summary: Spain is easing proposed rules for data centers after an initial plan faced strong industry backlash, giving operators as long as five years to phase in the government’s toughest renewable-energy requirement, according to a draft seen by Bloomberg.

title: Dutch Plan to Cut 25,000 Jobs Will Show Whether AI Can Shrink Government
summary: The Dutch government’s AI-led efficiency drive to cut 25,000 civil servant jobs is perhaps the most ambitious government plan yet to use tech to reduce the state’s payroll. Making it work — and rolling out similar programs in other countries — could prove tricky.

title: Memory Stocks Lost Their Mojo and Strong Earnings Aren’t Helping
summary: Sandisk Corp., Micron Technology Inc., Seagate Technology Holdings Plc and Western Digital Corp. were among the stock market’s biggest winners in the first six months of the year as demand from the artificial intelligence build out seemed insatiable.

title: Anduril and Qualcomm Plan US Supply Chain Laptop
summary: Anduril Industries and Qualcomm are producing laptops designed and assembled in the US, called BlueChip, to supply critical industries. Ed Ludlow has more on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Disruptive Closes $10 Billion Megafund for AI, Defense Startups
summary: The Dallas-based firm plans to back 10 later-stage companies with $1 billion each.

title: Apple Launches M6 iMac, Entry MacBook Pro Ahead of Touch Laptop
summary: Apple Inc. rolled out a new 24-inch iMac and an entry-level MacBook Pro with a 14-inch screen, marking a pair of key updates in an end-to-end overhaul of the company’s computer line.

title: Anduril and Qualcomm Plan to Build Laptop With US Supply Chain
summary: Defense tech startup Anduril Industries Inc. has joined forces with chipmaker Qualcomm Inc. to produce laptops that are designed and assembled in the US, an attempt to rebuild a manufacturing process that has largely moved overseas.

title: Healthcare Stocks Become Anti-AI Bet as Investors Turn Defensive
summary: With investor confidence in the artificial intelligence trade under pressure, traders are turning to healthcare stocks for refuge.

title: FCC Warns TP-Link Its Routers Breach Power Limits in Latest Snub
summary: The Federal Communications Commission has told TP-Link Systems Inc. that some of its Wi-Fi routers are violating power level limits, a move that could pave the way for additional bans on the California-based tech company’s equipment.

title: Intel to Buy Quantum Startup Classiq for About $2.3 Billion
summary: Intel Corp. agreed to buy Israeli startup Classiq Technologies Ltd. as part of a push to capitalize on quantum computing, a still-nascent field that is seeking commercial applications.

title: AI Circular Deals: How Microsoft, OpenAI and Nvidia Keep Paying Each Other
summary: A web of interlinked investments raises the risk of cascading losses if AI falls short of its potential.

title: Anthropic Relies on Close Connections With Amazon, Google and Microsoft
summary: Amazon and Google invested in the AI startup, supply it computing power — and compete with it.

title: Anthropic IPO Filing Reveals $417 Billion in Future AI Spending
summary: Anthropic just filed for one of the biggest IPOs in history – and may need more money.

title: Microsoft Alumni Score Funding to Build AI Agents for Finance
summary: Hyphenate Inc. has raised $45 million in a funding round led by Nexus Venture Partners, securing capital for an effort to create AI agents that can run finances for businesses.

title: Applied Materials Boosts BE Semiconductor Stake to About 20%
summary: Applied Materials Inc. boosted its stake in fellow chip-equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries NV and said it plans to work more closely with the European company, which is becoming a more important part of the AI computing supply chain.

title: JPMorgan Private Bank on How to Balance AI Exposure
summary: Madison Faller, investment strategist at JPMorgan Private Bank, says investors can balance AI exposure with quality credit and real assets. She speaks on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: SK Hynix, Samsung, Kioxia, CXMT Earnings Test AI Boom in Memory Market
summary: From South Korea to Japan and China, the world’s biggest memory chipmakers will this week seek to quell fears that AI spending is outpacing future demand. How they handle back-to-back earnings disclosures and investors’ questions will help determine the trajectory for markets and shed light on the broader outlook for the artificial intelligence industry.

title: How XDS Datacentres Cools Its Chips in Saudi Arabia
summary:
How do you keep a data center cool in Saudi Arabia? That's one of the questions Ikaraam Ullah, chief strategy officer at XDS Datacentres, answers in this interview at the BloombergNEF Summit London on Oct. 20, 2026.

Ullah also discusses recent tensions the Gulf region and the impact on data center operators, and how retrofitting existing facilities can help firms tackle issues over their power and water use in the UK and elsewhere in Europe. (Source: Bloomberg)
